post.hook: AI proof verified, Anthropic goes public
post.subhook: Plus Qwen4-Max, inference key theft and banks blocking agents

stories.headline: Lean community confirms Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof
stories.detail: Independent verifiers checked the Lean proof, so AI-assisted work on a famous open problem is now confirmed, not just claimed.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO opens about 34% above offer price on Nasdaq
stories.detail: A record listing for a frontier lab that has raised $81.3B. Its finances are now public and may shape how investors value AI companies.

stories.headline: Alibaba widely releases Qwen4-Max, reported at 2.4T parameters
stories.detail: Alibaba claims better coding and reasoning, giving developers another very large model option for those workloads.

stories.headline: Cheap inference resellers caught stealing API keys
stories.detail: Researchers show resellers reading requests and taking keys; OpenRouter removed three providers and 125 endpoints. Audit your providers.

stories.headline: Major US banks block third-party AI agents from customer logins
stories.detail: Banks say bot mistakes are the customer's problem, limiting what agent builders can automate in finance.

stories.headline: METR: models are improving faster than safety tests can measure
stories.detail: METR says current evaluations cannot rule out dangerous acceleration, so safety assessments may lag capability.

stories.headline: Coding agents finish under 1 in 10 tasks in a simulated workplace
stories.detail: Agents pass isolated tests but struggle with ongoing project work, well below what standalone benchmarks suggest.

stories.headline: MiniMax publishes AI-discovered cryptographic attacks with code
stories.detail: Papers and code are out, so security researchers can test the attacks themselves.

stories.headline: Perplexity launches Monitor API for scheduled web searches
stories.detail: Agents get webhook alerts only on relevant changes, so always-on monitoring no longer needs polling.

post.caption:
A Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis has been confirmed by the Lean and Mathlib community, and Anthropic is now a public company. Here is what changed today.

1. Lean and Mathlib verifiers confirm a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Source: The Decoder
2. Anthropic completes a record IPO, with shares opening about 34% above the offer price on Nasdaq. Source: CIO Africa
3. Alibaba widely releases Qwen4-Max, reported at 2.4 trillion parameters, claiming better coding and reasoning. Source: Vietnam.vn
4. Researchers show cheap inference resellers stealing API keys and reading requests; OpenRouter removed three providers and 125 endpoints. Source: The Decoder
5. Major US banks ban third-party AI agents from logging into customer accounts. Source: WIRED
6. METR warns frontier models are improving faster than safety tests can measure. Source: The Decoder
7. Coding agents finish fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated developer workplace. Source: The Decoder
8. MiniMax publishes AI-discovered cryptographic attacks with papers and code. Source: TechNode
9. Perplexity launches a Monitor API with webhook alerts on relevant web changes. Source: The Decoder

If you route traffic through a cheap inference provider, audit it today. 🔐

clusters.headline: Anthropic-affiliated mathematician's Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis is confirmed by the Lean and Mathlib community
clusters.why_it_matters: Independent verifiers checked the Lean proof, so AI-assisted work on a famous open problem is now confirmed rather than only claimed.

clusters.headline: Anthropic completes a record IPO and shares open about 34% above the offer price on Nasdaq
clusters.why_it_matters: The listing of a leading frontier lab with $81.3B raised makes its finances public and is likely to shape how investors value AI companies.

clusters.headline: Alibaba widely releases its Qwen4-Max model, reported at 2.4 trillion parameters, with claims of better coding and reasoning
clusters.why_it_matters: A widely released very large model from a major provider gives developers another option for coding and reasoning workloads.

clusters.headline: Security researchers show cheap AI inference resellers steal API keys and read customer requests; OpenRouter removes three providers and 125 endpoints
clusters.why_it_matters: Teams routing traffic through cheap inference providers may have leaked AWS keys and exposed prompts, so they should audit their providers.

clusters.headline: Major US banks ban third-party AI agents from logging into customer accounts and say bot mistakes are the customer's problem
clusters.why_it_matters: Agents that act through customer logins will lose access to major bank accounts, which limits what agent builders can automate in finance.

clusters.headline: METR warns that frontier models are improving faster than safety tests can measure them
clusters.why_it_matters: METR says current evaluations cannot rule out dangerous acceleration, so safety assessments may lag behind model capability.

clusters.headline: AI coding agents pass isolated tests but finish fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated developer workplace
clusters.why_it_matters: Teams relying on coding agents for ongoing project work should expect much lower completion than standalone benchmarks suggest.

clusters.headline: MiniMax publishes AI-discovered cryptographic attacks with papers and code
clusters.why_it_matters: Published attack code and papers let security researchers test cryptographic systems that AI discovered.
